The second quarter marked a strong recovery from disruptions witnessed in Q1 of this year. We 
delivered double-digit quarter-on-quarter growth in both sales volume and net revenue, 
supported by a high share of value-added products, driven by the strong momentum in 
automotive and ornamental pipe and tube segments.  
Turning to market demand, domestic demand remained healthy across our key end-user 
segments, including automotive, railways, metros, lifts, elevators, and white goods. This was

supported by robust economic growth and an increasing awareness about lifecycle costing. We 
also witnessed global acceptance of plates and ferritic grades across white goods and lift and

On the international front, exports recorded strong growth both sequentially and year-on-year, 
reflecting our continued focus on market diversification. We are expanding our presence across 
markets, including South Korea, Colombia, South Africa, Brazil, and Japan as we continue to 
pursue value-added opportunities globally.  
On the operational front, industrial gas availability remained stable during Q2, with no 
reoccurrence of the challenges experienced in the previous quarter. We continue to be watchful 
of developments on this front as uncertainties continue to resurface. Amidst this, our transition 
to natural gas has strengthened operational resilience, supporting uninterrupted operations.  
Alongside strengthening our presence in established segments, we continue to expand our 
product portfolio, and develop new applications for stainless steel. Key achievements include 
the development of India's first high-aluminum stainless steel grade for catalytic converters and 
development of two new 400 series grades, one of which has opened up a new market in South 
Africa. 
Additionally, we entered into a technical assistance agreement with Japan's JFE Steel for 
selected ferritic grades, further strengthening our technical capabilities. During the quarter, we 
also made progress on strengthening our corporate structure and credit profile.  
The board approved the amalgamation of four wholly owned subsidiaries into Jindal Stainless 
Limited, a step towards simplifying our group structure and enhancing operational efficiency 
and governance as well. Further, CARE Ratings upgraded our long-term debt credit rating to 
AA+ Stable. 
On brand and customer engagement, we continue to expand our reach through our pipe and tube 
campaign. With airport branding at Delhi and Mumbai airports and influencer-led digital 
outreach, we also expanded our brand ambassador, Ranveer Singh's, presence across partner 
packaging and marketing collaterals. Our Jindal Saathi loyalty program continued to gain 
traction amongst retailers and fabricators, receiving gold and silver awards at the ET Brand 
Equity MarTech and DigiPlus awards.  
The Saathi Seal co-branding initiative was also extended to water tanks, strengthening our 
engagement with channel partners. We have made further progress in skill development and 
digitalization. Stainless academy signed an agreement with NCVET for recognition as an 
awarding body, paving the way for government-recognized certification programs for the 
stainless steel ecosystem.  
Our B2B platform achieved full digital adoption among MOU trade and plates and tube 
manufacturing partners. In addition, Jindal Lifestyle commissioned a new powder coating 
facility at Pathredi to cater to metro and infrastructure applications. Sustainability remains an 
integral part of our long-term strategy. During the quarter, we reduced our Scope 1 and Scope 2

The domestic market continued to face import pressure. Since April 2026 following the 
suspension of the quality control order, imports of substandard products, particularly from China 
and of Chinese origin, have increased significantly. Chinese origin imports during the first 4 
months of the current fiscal year alone were equivalent to nearly two-thirds of the total imports 
recorded during the previous fiscal year. We believe that maintaining consistent quality 
standards is essential for public safety, product reliability and fair competition. We remain 
hopeful that the regulatory framework will evolve to appropriately balance consumer interests, 
the competitiveness of domestic manufacturers and the broader economic interest.  
 
To conclude, Q2 reflects our ability to recover from near-term disruptions while continuing to 
strengthen our business for the long term. We remain focused on expanding our market reach, 
developing new applications, improving our product mix, and deepening our presence across 
domestic and international markets. We remain confident in the long-term growth opportunities 
for stainless steel.

from earlier INR18,000 to INR20,000 a ton. The capex and net debt guidance range remains

reduce administrative and compliance costs, eliminate intercompany transactions and balances
